item.title: Strasbourg: Capital de Noël
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Strasbourg is by far the most beautiful city I've ever been to on a Christmas season. It lived up to its name, Capital de Noël or the Christmas Capital. The city is known for its annual Christmas market which started all the way back from the 16th century, making it one of the oldest Christmas markets in Europe. Probably it's just me, but the city gives the Christmas vibe straight out of the movies. Walking on a cold night at the centuries-old cobbled stone street; Christmas music playing in the background; sipping a cup of vin chaud. You know what I mean. It was just sad when a few weeks before our visit, there was a mass shooting happened in the Christmas market which killed five and injuring several. Despite what had happened, the people of Strasbourg displayed their resilience and resumed the festive season welcoming hundreds of thousands of tourists from around the world. Europe has a lot of Christmas capitals in different countries and we're definitely looking forward to visiting if not all, but most of them. :) [caption id="attachment_5250" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Buildings decorated with teddy bears[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5251" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Teddy bear waiting for hugs ;)[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5257" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Perspective :3[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5256" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Looks like they're about to drop the hottest album of the year[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5255" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Memorial for the victims of the terrorist attack[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5254" align="aligncenter" width="860"] White or Red? item.title: Around Paris on Holiday Season
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: For our Christmas holiday vacation, we stayed in Paris. Thanks to our good friend Hanna, who let us stay at her place, we were able to save some of our expenses. Within our two week vacation, we went to Strasbourg, Bordeaux, and Disneyland. Thus, Paris was strategically perfect for us. While we were there, we managed to explore around Paris. We went to grab some hot wine and tasted some French delicacies at the Christmas market together with our friend, Bere. Took some pictures at the Louvre. Checked out the colorful Christmas tree inside the Galeries Lafayette and went up to the rooftop to see Paris from above. We walked around Eiffel Tower at night, just like the scenes of those romantic movies. But it was freaking cold, so yeah... not what we had expected. We went up to Sacre Coeur since it's just next to where we stayed. Passed by the Place du Tertre where artists gather and display their unbelievable artworks. Sacre Coeur is one of the highest points in Paris. If you want to see the endless horizon of Paris, this is one of the best places to go. The New Year countdown was tempting. And who wouldn't love to see it in person when your only memory of watching it was through TV on the other side of the world. However, we decided to stay. The Gilets Jaunes protests were active that time. We thought there were a lot of things that could go wrong. Better safe than sorry. Maybe next time. ;) Overall, we had a good time. No one got sick. Well, I did but I managed. :D [caption id="attachment_5272" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Rue de la Paix, a street near the Opera House[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5264" align="aligncenter" width="860"] The Opera House and the rugged faces[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5263" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Avenue de l'Opéra[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5277" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Christmas market near Place de la Concorde[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5276" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Raclette: One of the best foods that I can never have.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5273" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Sausage party[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5274" align="aligncenter" width="860"] I forgot what is this, probably duck.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5275" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Happy kids[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5265" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Heavy traffic also exists in Paris. ;) Viewed at the top of the Galeries Lafayette[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5266" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Christmas tree inside Galeries Lafayette[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5267" align="aligncenter" width="860"] The grand Eiffel Tower at night[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5269" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Artist's work[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5270" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Paris horizon[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5271" align="aligncenter" width="860"] The Sacre Coeur[/caption]

item.title: Disneyland Paris: Waking Up The Kid Inside
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Before our vacation was over, we decided to visit Disneyland. Iris has been there once while I had never been to any amusement park prior to my stay here in Europe. Aside from seeing Mickey Mouse and all other childhood stars, I had no other expectations on what to do there. When we arrived, I would never have imagined that for a minute, fairy tales could come true. Yeah, sounds cheesy but the feeling was surreal when we were inside the Disney village (or whatever its name). All those shops, houses, and streets have seemed like pulled out straight from the TV and turned into a reality. If you remember your childhood memories where you imagine yourself living in this made up utopia, then being here is (almost) exactly it, except that it only lasts a day. There were a lot of rides to choose from but considering the length of the queue per ride, it’s impossible to try them all in one day. We’ve only managed to ride few of them, you know, the essentials. Surprisingly, I enjoyed the “It’s A Small World” ride and for the first time in a long time, I finally tried the “Merry go round“. Bucket list, checked! But the most extreme was the “Indiana Jones” roller coaster. That was definitely something. But the highlight of the trip was the parade of stars where every character is trying to wake up the kid inside you. At night, the village turned from perfect into magical. And of course, the fireworks that light up the famous castle. item.title: Quick Hike Through The Slopes of Verbier
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Every year, Batmaid organize an annual team building held in Verbier, one of the top ski resorts in Switzerland. The last time I was here 2 years ago, I experienced snow for the first time. :D We spent the weekend at the resort having fun. Skiing here for sure would be so much fun if I know how to. But even if I have the skill, I would still rather not due to fact that it's quite expensive. :P However, there is a cheaper and equally fun to do; sledging. I didn't have proper gears last time so I stopped after two rounds because my toes are freezing. I was not briefed what to wear for the winter. ;) But this time, I came with proper clothes. There was one problem though. The slopes were closed due to insufficient amount of snow. Dang! So, the group decided to go on a quick hike in the mountains to kill the time. The trail was easy but it gets tricky when you don't have enough sleep. :P The vin chaud at the end of the trail did help. ;) [caption id="attachment_5306" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Skiers preparing to go down[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5307" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Looks like a movie scene. ;)[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5308" align="aligncenter" width="860"] On our way to the white jungle :D[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5309" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Skiers and hikers[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5310" align="aligncenter" width="860"] We also met hikers going opposite to our direction[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5311" align="aligncenter" width="860"] And on our way too.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5312" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Daily scrum :P[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5315" align="aligncenter" width="860"] No idea what to do with my hands :D[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5316" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Dominik preparing for the front roll[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5317" align="aligncenter" width="860"] The Beatles :P[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5318" align="aligncenter" width="860"] Saved by the Hot Wines[/caption]

item.title: Hiking Along Lac Léman
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: The original plan was to hike up to Rochers de Naye but unfortunately, the tourism office closed it for hikers due to heavy snow. So we just decided to walk along the lake and from Villeneuve, go up to a vantage point overlooking the Lac Léman. We started our hike at the vineyards in Lutry. I've been there in summer two years ago and definitely was one of the best view I've seen. However, it's a bit dry this time since it was still winter. After an hour or two, we took a train to Montreux, where supposedly our starting point to the mountain. But since we were not allowed to go up, we just decided to walk along the lake until Villeneuve. Imagine four grown men walking along a beautiful lake on a sunny day. Isn't it romantic? ;) Surprisingly, the scenery was stunning. Probably, Lac Léman is the clearest and cleanest lake I've ever seen. Spending summer here will be absolutely perfect, specially when I saw a diving board on the side of the lake. :P We ended our hike halfway from the vantage point we're planning to go to because it was already dark and nobody brought any flashlights. item.title: Darwin: A Hidden Hip Place of Bordeaux
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: I've been to Bordeaux a couple of times but it was the first time I've heard of Darwin when Iris brought me there, together with her friend all the way from Manila and the other one from Barcelona. Darwin environment is completely opposite from the typical grandiose 18th century urban architecture of Bordeaux. Here, you can see the hippie and rebellious vibes. A place where graffiti, skateboarding, food and workplace co-exists in harmony. There are even small apartments inside the compound for those who want to spend a night or two here. Skateboarders of no age limit have their place inside the buildings with complete ramps. Graffiti artists display their works on the walls. Professionals work in a co-working place although I am not sure if there are many start-ups currently based here. And of course, this place is not complete without food. If you just want coffee or up for some burgers, pizzas and more, Darwin has it. By the time we visited Darwin, it was obviously still under development but it's quite interesting how it will look like in the future. item.title: Epic (Fail) Surfing in Siargao
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: My first attempt on surfing was in Dulag Surf Camp which obviously didn't turn out well as I had imagined. Here in Siargao is my second try and confident enough that it will be much better than before. And of course, it was not. :P We surfed three days in a row which for me was not enough. I could spend at least a month there doing nothing but surfing (I wish). Compared to Dulag, Siargao is more dangerous not just because of the waves and sharp rocks but also of the crowd. There were at least 30 people trying to catch the same wave. Of course, accidents are prone to happen. And I do had my fair share of injury. I got hit by a kid with his short board (see short clip below). Good thing it was the side of the board that hit my knee. If it was the pointed tip, it would have been another story. But injuries and wounds aside, our experience was so much fun. Surfing is challenging and exhausting but has a different level of fun. However, it is quite expensive specially if you don't have your own board and if you need a guide. And speaking of guide, we highly recommend Kuya Roel, who was our guide for three days, a nice and experienced surfer. If you're going to Siargao soon, don't hesitate to contact him through his mobile number (+63907 140 4532). item.title: The Elusive Island of Siargao
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: It has been a long time since I've been wanting to go to Siargao. In fact, three years ago I had two tickets for Siargao, a plane ticket I got from airfare promo and a boat ticket I bought when I knew that my friends were also going on a separate date. Unfortunately, all those tickets went to nowhere but in a hospital. On the day of my flight, I was admitted to a hospital due to sever sore throat. And there goes my Siargao. Gone. :D Three years later and finally, I was able to check it off of my list. We spent four days doing nothing but surfing and living the island life. ;) Just kidding! I was actually tip-tapping my keyboard hoping to get some job done remotely and Iris was working on her thesis but actually, nothing much were done because of the turtle speed internet. A friendly island reminder that you don't have to bring your work when in Siargao. People say that Siargao has now become crowded compared to few years back. And in fact, the crowd is noticeably visible, most of them are international tourists. It is highly possible that the arrival of increasingly number of tourists will lead to an undesirable damage of the island. Fortunately, the people in the island are already aware of this and are making great effort to handle the situation. One exceptional example is the ban on single use plastics. Everybody is encourage to bring their own bags whenever they go to the market and recycle whatever can be recycled. So for you out there who are planning to visit Siargao, you know what to do. Actually, let's be responsible wherever we go, not just in Siargao because the truth is, all these islands are on the same planet. ;) Cheers! item.title: Hong Kong In Less Than An Hour
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Travelling sleep deprived is worst. Travelling with diarrhea is on another level. It's a nightmare. We intentionally booked a connecting flight in Hong Kong going back to Warsaw with enough layover time to roam around the city. Everything was according to plan until few minutes before boarding time for Hong Kong. My intestines started a coup. I thought a simple chug of a trusted tablet would stop it. And it did, for few hours. :( We arrived in Hong Kong desperately looking for the nearest toilet. At that time, going to the city center became the least priority. We were about to stay at the airport and wait for our next flight but I felt inner peace and calmness after some rest. So f*ck it, Hong Kong is waiting for us. We took the express train for convenience. But as soon as we arrived in Kowloon, it started again. Have you ever had that goosebumps feeling while your blood is slowly draining down from your face and any body movement could potentially cause an instant embarrassment? That the only thing you care about is to wish that you're at home comfortably sitting on that throne? That was me, sitting still on the bench, hopeless and trying not to cry. :D After Iris took a few photos of the harbor, we decided to go back to the airport immediately. We figured, we can still go back here in the future without my dignity on the line. By the way, I suffered for another 15 hours before we safely arrived in Warsaw. I guess we can call it a different kind of mile high experience. ;) [caption id="attachment_5431" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] The famous high rise buildings along Victoria Harbour[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5438" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Hong Kong - Central[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5432" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Center[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5436" align="alignnone" width="1024"] The iconic Aqua Luna red sail junk boat[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5434" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Hong Kong - Wan Chai[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5439" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Iris is fond of building patterns[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5433" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Harbour Promenade[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5440" align="alignnone" width="1024"] The face of suffering[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5437" align="alignnone" width="1024"] On to my next 15 hours of torture[/caption]

item.title: Warsaw from the High Ground
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: A friend of my office mate invited us to take a look at the new building which is expected to be one of the highest in Europe. I do have a fear of heights, specially climbing on a makeshift stairs hanging out 30 floors above the ground but it's always what's up there that makes every nerve-racking step worth it. The gorgeous night scenery of Warsaw. I've been wanting to take photos of Warsaw at night from above. Although, the Palace of Culture and Science tower is available for it, this one is better because there are less barriers. Currently, the building is halfway. Twenty floors more and Varso Place will become the highest office building in Europe. The director explained a lot of details on how the construction was going on that would have been interesting but unfortunately, nie mówię po polsku. When this building is finished, it is expected to draw some attention. And for sure, this will be added to Warsaw's tourist destinations. item.title: A Short Walk Along Nowy Świat
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
It was a cold, dull late afternoon when I decided to grab my camera and went for a short walk at Nowy Świat street towards the Old Town. The street is pretty bright this time of the year because of the lights for the Christmas season. I've wanted to do this for years, but I was just too lazy to do it. But hey, you can't blame me, it's freezing outside. However, this time is different. It's warmer than the previous years. Yeah man, climate change is f***ing real.

To be honest, I was a bit disappointed when I reached the Christmas market at the Old Town Square. I was expecting a more festive and crowded market with a sea of food stalls, but it was not. Or maybe my expectation just went higher after my visit to Strasbourg the other year.

Anyway, I didn't stay long because it was getting colder that night. It would have been easier and have better photos if I had a tripod. Without it, I am usually on my Slavic Squat, waiting for the shutter. To be fair, I think my squatting game was pretty spot on. ;) Peace out!

wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Remember: when Slavs squat around, heels touch the ground

item.title: La Grande Arche de la Défense
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: The Great Arch of the Defense is located in the business district of La Défense. A 110-meter-high cube, La Grande Arche is part of the perspective from the Louvre to Arc de Triomphe. The building is mostly occupied by government offices, but the roof deck is open to the public that features a restaurant, an art gallery, and a panoramic view of Paris. Most of the time, the weather in Paris is gloomy. But the day we went up there was the complete opposite. Going up to the rooftop was a little edgy, with an elevator made of glass, and looking down while inside the lift could be terrifying, especially to an acrophobic like me. However, the view over Paris and the intense color of the sunset erased all that. The panorama is stunning. Paris glows at night. If not for the biting cold and hunger, we could have stayed longer. :P [caption id="attachment_5487" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Defense 2000 - A residential building[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5490" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] The skating rink is seemingly made of plastic instead of ice. I'm not sure though. :P[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5486" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] The buildings at the business district all the way to downtown Paris[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5492" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Sunset and the moon[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5491" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Société Générale Twin Towers[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5489" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] On the to the skating rink[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5493" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Eiffel Tower is lurking behind[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5494" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] The avenue will lead straight to Arc de Triomphe and Louvre Museum through Av. des Champs-Élysées[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5485" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] La Grande Arche de la Défense[/caption]

item.title: Seine River Cruise in Paris
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: We had been to Paris a couple of times, but we never had the chance to hop on the river cruise. Well, typically, because we thought the distance covered is not worth the price. But this time, the tickets were free. I mean, nobody says no for free stuff, right? Big thanks to Iris' friends who gave the tickets as a gift for our wedding. The cruise was okay. Well, aside from the fact that it's Paris, there was not much special about it, probably because it's winter when everything is grey. You're just sitting by the window (if you're lucky to get in first) staring at other people's backs who are brave enough to stay out in the cold. I'm sure the view is different compared to summertime, where people are chilling by the river banks (if not blasting their speakers to some trap music). If the water level is low enough, it is allowed to stay on the roof deck for the entire duration of the cruise where you can have a 360 view of the river. If you're lucky to do this, maybe you'll get what you paid for. Overall, it was a nice experience. The only bad thing that happened was when they shut down the metro line. We either had to walk or wait for the limited bus and packed like canned sardines. item.title: Randomness Around Paris
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: RATP, the public transport operator in Paris, stopped its operation most of the time in the last quarter of 2019 until early this year. Because of this, you'll often end up walking long distances around for sightseeing which is what we did. Along with it were fun experiences and exhausted legs. One of them was the pickpocket attempt. We were walking towards the Christmas market with our backpacks when we noticed that there were two guys behind us trying to unzip one of our bags. Good thing Iris was quick enough to turn her back and for a split-second, there was a confusing awkwardness between us and them. And then they took off as nothing happened. And we realized, yep, just like home. :D Another thing was my first-time experience with Grande Roue de Paris or the Ferris wheel. I am not a big fan of heights, especially dangling 60 meters above the ground. It was one of those experiences where one is enough. :P We also stroll along Champs-Élysées, where you can find the definition of capitalism. :D If you're into buying expensive luxury stuff, you belong here. One thing that caught my attention was inside the Apple store. I saw a young girl bought a brand new iPhone with cash. While she's counting, I noticed an old lady next to her whom I assumed is her grandmother. Of course, I don't know their story but I just can't help to picture out the situation in my mind and it's a pity. Or maybe I just saw too many shit stories on the internet that lead me to this conclusion. Ooooorrrr... I'm just jealous because I can't afford to buy an iPhone. *cries in silence* Overall, we had fun. We went home tired, exhausted and starving. o.O [caption id="attachment_5522" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Christmas market at La Defense[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5523" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Eiffel Tower viewed from Grande Roue de Paris[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5524" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Typical Paris from above[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5525" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Me trying not to shit bricks as the wind blows by[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5517" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] The least thing you can do for things you can't afford: stare.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5520" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Gucci Gang[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5518" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Pro[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5521" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Just passing by[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5526" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] La Defense business district[/caption]

item.title: Sunset in Lausanne
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Every year, we go to Batmaid's HQ in Lausanne for our annual gathering or sort of team building to meet other members of the company from different offices. We usually stay there for the entire week, working on weekdays and go up the mountains on the weekend for the anticipated party. It is often gloomy and rainy in Lausanne during winter, but that day, I have never seen a beautiful sunset over the lake. And it's been a long time since I saw one. I went down to the lake to take a couple of pictures and to relax. It is nice to pause and calm down from time to time. You know, forget everything for a second to focus at the moment and wonder: a swan floating carefree on the lake waiting for its dinner, probably has a better life than most of us? :thinking emoji: It was a great day, but I couldn't stay long because it was getting cold. I went home and had a good sleep, prepared for the grind the next day. ;) [caption id="attachment_5536" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Lausanne Gare[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5534" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Trains departing and arriving to Lausanne Gare[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5538" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Irony[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5539" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Social distancing before it was mandatory. item.title: Once Again, Verbier
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: It was my third time to be in Verbier. It has been the go-to destination on every Batmaid's annual team gathering with more people every year than the previous ones. Having been here a couple of times, I already had ideas on what will happen over the weekend. That's why I took a rest most of the day at the hotel. But for some reason, I have trouble sleeping every time we're here. So, I decided to skip the hike organized by the team. But I had to admit, I regretted not doing it, especially when I saw their pictures. I mean, how often could you visit one of the top winter destinations in Switzerland for free? Also, trying to sleep at the hotel didn't pay off because I ended up staying awake the whole time. So I just decided to go out and walked around taking pictures which could have been better if I was at the top of the mountain. :| However, the real fun happened on our last night at Verbier. We sledded down to our hotel from the restaurant on the hill where we had our dinner. You may say sledging is not as cool as skiing but make no mistake, we did it at night on almost zero visibility and drunk. Well, most of us were. It was fun to the point where it almost crossed the boundary of serious injuries. :D In the end, everybody arrived at the hotel with bruises, wet, semi-frost bites, and with twelve sledges missing. ;) [caption id="attachment_5562" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Fog[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5561" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Chalets[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5560" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Snowless road[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5559" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Cable cars[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5556" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Sitting in peace[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5558" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Chalets at the base of the mountain[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5554" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Skier[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5552" align="alignnone" width="1200"] Man on parachute[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5553" align="alignnone" width="1024"] Premium Batmaid bus which took us from Verbier straight to Geneva airport[/caption]

item.title: ATV Ride at Bohol's Chocolate Hills
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: I've been to these famous hills even before it gained popularity among local and international tourists. In fact, my grandparent's house was literally on top of a hill. Chocolate hills are scattered throughout three towns but the famous attraction is in Carmen. As the hills became more popular, the number of activities offered to tourists also increased. One of them is ATV ride that goes through the foothills. It would be unwise not to try it. So we did. We rode through the terrain for about an hour with stops on selected spots for a couple of pictures. Each group is assigned with a tour guide and included on his services is being a photographer. These guys have templates on what pose is good for which background. And you are obliged to do so. :D It was fun but I would advise to do it early in the morning or late in the afternoon unless you want to suffer from 32 degrees under the sun. ;) [caption id="attachment_5577" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Sassy and poised[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5579" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Controlling this ATV isn't as easy at it looks :P[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5580" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Cruisin'[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5578" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Believe it or not, this is one of the guide's template pose. :D[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5574" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] o.O[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5576" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Iris and Kristy[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5575" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] This right here...[/caption]

item.title: Arcachon, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
The last time I'd been to the beach was almost a year ago. And as a sucker for beach or any particular places near the sea, it has been a long wait for me.

When the EU opened its borders again, I immediately visited Iris and went to Arcachon for a weekend. I badly needed this to decompress and reset for a little bit. Some of you might say that my complaint is nothing compared to most of the people badly affected by the pandemic. I totally agree and I'm aware of it. But I don't have to explain myself. ;)

I don't know if I'm the only one who felt this but there is something about the sea that relaxes you and takes some heavy load off of you. Early morning dip was perfect, not only because of cold water but also, the beach was empty.

Although the visit was short, it was enough for me to refocus and go back hustling again. Next time, it's going to be longer. ;)

item.title: Dune Du Pilat, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Dune du Pilat, also called as Grande Dune du Pilat, is the tallest sand dune in Europe, with the height of 106.60m above sea level (as of 2018). It is located in La Teste-de-Buch in the Arcachon Bay area, France, just 60 km from Bordeaux. We took a few-hour side trip during our trip to Arcachon since it's just less than an hour away from the town. The dune has a massive area that it's better to take a drone to appreciate its grandness (although I don't think it is legal to fly a drone here without a permit). Based on experience, you need to have enough stamina to walk up the dune, if you are not planning to take the stairs. Also, it is probably better to visit in the morning or late in the afternoon unless you enjoy the scorching hot sun and sand. Most of the people go there to enjoy the stunning view overlooking the Atlantic Ocean. But the most famous activity here is paragliding. So if you're into it, you're in for a treat. item.title: Fontainebleau, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Year 2020 has been, to put it delicately, weirdly fucked up. The pandemic has changed, if not lost, a lot of lives, and in fact, it still is. Normally, Iris and I are going somewhere for vacation around this time. However, everything was put on hold since the virus had a different plan for everyone. The pictures on this post were taken four months ago, just weeks before the second lockdown. We were able to walk around Fontainebleau for a couple of hours to break from our daily routine of waking up, eat breakfast, and work at the same place. And before one of you start bitching about staying home, yes you're right and yes, we took extra precautionary measures to be safe as much as possible. ;) In fact, we really didn't stay for long to avoid the crowd and went home as soon as it started to get cold. Although the pandemic forced us to take a different course, I'm not in the position to complain. Having a stable job when majority of the people lost theirs is already a huge bonus. So if you are reading this at your apartment, warm and cozy, stop being pessimistic but instead be grateful and if possible, help someone you know who is struggling. item.title: Antibes, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: How long has it been? :P After over a year, we were able to go out again, at least for now. But before anything else, we need to set the record straight. We were fully vaccinated, wore masks on crowded areas and took proper distancing as much as possible. ;) Iris and I took a few days of holidays and went to Nice (again). Since we have plenty of time, we managed to go on day trips in the neighboring cities along Côte d'Azur. Today, we went to Antibes. It is a resort town between Cannes and Nice.  It’s known for its old town enclosed by 16th-century ramparts with the star-shaped Fort Carré (wiki). However, I would describe it as a town of luxury and superyachts. There's just too many of them docked at Port Vauban. Aside from the mind blowing yachts, there's also a Picasso Museum which housed his artworks. The old town streets are definitely instagrammable so wandering around can be quite pleasant. However, we couldn't bare the scorching heat of the sun. Summer here can be brutal. So the plan of going to Cannes afterwards was abandoned. Instead, we went home to Nice and enjoyed the very much needed airconditioned room. :P [caption id="attachment_5713" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Port Vauban[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5712" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] What else is missing on a superyacht? item.title: Menton, France

item.title: Monte Carlo, Monaco
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Monaco is just few minutes train ride from Nice. The last time we were here, we only went to the marina since we had limited time. This time, we had our full day to spend exploring Monaco. The same as before, nothing has changed. Everywhere you look, everything is expensive. If you hate money, this is the right place to get rid of it. :P There were quite a lot of people here which got me wondering, are these rich people or are they just like us who are curious of what luxury looks like? :thinking-face: Whichever it is, they sure are in the right place. After we took off from the train, we walked downhill straight to Grimaldi Forum where the arts of Alberto Giacometti were displayed and stayed a little bit on their small Japanese garden before lunch. Normally, I wouldn't care going to a restaurant with just t-shirt, shorts and sneakers on. What's important is that, I can pay. However, it just doesn't work in Monaco. If you don't own at least a yacht and a lambo, something's in your head telling you, "You don't belong here, peasant. Go find your way to McDonald's". And yes we did. :D And on our way, we heard a familiar language. Wherever we go, it's guaranteed to meet Filipinos. That moment when you locked eyes and simultaneously raised your both eyebrows feels different. Normally, I wouldn't care going to a restaurant with just t-shirt, shorts and sneakers on. What's important is that, I can pay. However, it just doesn't work in Monaco. If you don't own at least a yacht and a lambo, something's in your head telling you, "You don't belong here, peasant. Go find your way to McDonald's". And yes we did. :D

item.title: Nice, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: We stayed in Nice during our vacation for strategic reasons. It has convenient connections to the cities along the Mediterranean coast. On top of that, it has a long stretch of shoreline, although not a sandy beach, where we could eat our freshly baked le croissant or le pain au chocolat paired with cheap brewed coffee. Then swim late in the afternoon after walking all day. Out of all the places I've been to, Nice, in my opinion, is close to my ideal place to live. The beach and convenience are all in one place. Of course, this excludes all the shit shows that happened and is happening there. I'm a simple guy, put me next to any body of water and we're good. ;) To cap our vacation, we pampered ourselves with a spa and got the much needed massage. My back pain was killing me all year. P.S. All pictures here were taken by Iris on a disposable film camera. item.title: Lake Geneva, Switzerland
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Our annual company team gathering was postponed this year. The winter Verbier escapade was moved to summer in Lausanne. We were there for a couple of days together with Iris. One day before we went back to France, we took the cruise on Lake Geneva. I've been to Lausanne for a couple of times but I've never tried the cruise. Probably because I usually go to Lausanne in winter. And, well, aside from fact that, I don't like to be on it alone. :P There are many routes you can choose from but we took the one that starts from Lausanne to Chillon castle with three stops at St. Gingolph, Port-Valais and Villeneuve in between. It was a great experience and is highly recommended, on top of taking a dip on the lake, when you are about to visit Lausanne. item.title: Perpignan, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: We went down south for a weekend on Hannah's birthday. Perpignan, a small French city near the Mediterranean coast and the border with Spain, is more or less 6 hours train ride from Paris. There was really not much to do around the city. We went for the usual tourist routes and explore a little bit outside the city. There was a food event of some sort called Pyrénéon where we had our brunch. We went to the coast and stayed there for a couple of hours and had some drinks. Of course, the sea was a refreshing sight. Unfortunately, Iris and I had to leave early because we need to catch the last train going home. item.title: Dubai Expo 2020, UAE
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Few months prior to our vacation in UAE, we were discussing either we stay in Europe or fly out to UAE. Since the restrictions were eased out, we decided to go for UAE. Thanks to Iris' cousin, the von Kaufmann family, who hosted us during our trip. First on our list was to visit the Expo. Expo 2020 was supposed to be in 2020 but was postponed due to the pandemic. There are over a hundred country participants, each of them showcasing their country’s pride, ranging from foods, history, culture, and technology. The Expo was huge that we only covered few pavilions. One needs to spend maybe 2-3 full days to explore everything. UAE has huge Filipino communities specially in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. The whole time we were there, it feels like we were in the Philippines. Kabayans. Kabayans everywhere. :D We only visited the Expo once, not only to avoid the crowd, but also due to unexpected circumstances :P [caption id="attachment_5835" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] On our way to Philippine pavilion :D[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5836" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Pilipinas[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5837" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Next to Philippines is Canada[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5839" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Cultural show from Malaysia[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5838" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Expo's main stage for concerts and exhibitions[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5840" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Matrix-like shenanigans at Korea Pavilion[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5841" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Rooftop - Korean Pavilion[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5843" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Korean show aka BTS show[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5834" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Portugal pavilion, I think. :D[/caption] [caption id="attachment_5842" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] The Dome[/caption]

item.title: Liwa, UAE
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: After Christmas, Bruce and Ate Mae organized a three days, two nights camping in the desert. They had done it multiple times but it was our first time. I did camping a couple of times before but this was far different from those. In Liwa, you'll see nothing but sand, everywhere. If you've been to any campsite and spent at least one night, you know that it's the "number 2" you are most worried about. So, just imagine doing it in the desert where you have nothing to use as a cover. But aside from that, everything was an unforgettable experience. Surreal. From the toilet problem, to the absolutely delicious foods and most of all, the heart pumping buggy ride. It was an awesome adventure. Thanks to the von Kaufmann family for organizing it and for having us. C'était super ! [caption id="attachment_5861" align="aligncenter" width="1000"] We arrived at our first campsite. item.title: Abu Dhabi, AUE
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: We stayed in Abu Dhabi the whole time during our vacation. Aside from the Expo and the Liwa camping, we managed to visit some sites in Abu Dhabi. We went to the Louvre museum, fun ride at Warner Bros, Emirates Park Zoo, Abu Dhabi Grand Masjid but most of the time, we spent it going back and forth to get tested for Covid :P There are more things to do in the city specially if you like heart pumping rides. The extreme rides, specifically at the Ferrari World, are not for everyone and I'm pretty sure it's not for me. But it's a must try for every thrill seekers out there. If you have a chance to try it, please do try it. However, you might want to wait a little longer for the pandemic to end. item.title: Lyon, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Lyon, a 2 hour away via train, located southeast of Paris, is a city I've known from travel videos. It is known as food capital of France and so we went. Aside from food, it also has quite few sceneries, strolling in the old town, go up on a funicular or just chill on the riverbanks, they have two rivers, in fact. We met with Marie, Iris' classmate from her Masters II. She guided us around the city and of course, she brought us to one of the bouchons in Lyon, a restaurant which serves local cuisine. It was delicious and indeed, on a trop mangé. However, I would say we enjoyed more the unlimited Korean BBQ. item.title: Strasbourg, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Once again, we went to Strasbourg. The first time we were here was on Christmas day in 2018. The city is known as Christmas Capital and anyone who has a chance to visit here during this season must not have second thoughts. It's indeed truly amazing. I'm sure that our stay there would would have been more magical if not due to the mass shooting prior to our arrival. We chose to go back to the city since it has good connections to neighboring cities, specifically Colmar and Basel. We didn't spend much time here since we already walked mostly around the city before. Probably one of the highlights was whiskey tasting even though I had no idea what I was doing. item.title: Colmar, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: If Iris hadn't told me that the village in Beauty and The Beast was (most likely) inspired from Colmar, I wouldn't have any idea where Colmar is. The resemblance between the Disney movie and the city is uncanny. Dreamy colorful houses, cobblestone streets and quaint shops. If you've been to Disneyland, you would definitely feel that Disney-ish vibe (without the rides) just by walking around the old town. We only spent one whole day exploring the city since we stayed in Strasbourg but it was more than enough for classic tourists like ourselves. :P It was a nice experience except for the long waiting time during our lunch and aching knees and feet. Wear comfy shoes kids. item.title: Basel, Switzerland
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: The last city we went to for our side trips was Basel, Switzerland. It is just few minutes away from Colmar via train. I've been to Switzerland a couple of times before but mainly in the south. I could say that this country is no stranger to me, but every time I arrive at the airport or train stations, there is this different feeling where you must compose yourself on everything you do and wherever you go. Otherwise, you're in for trouble. Probably, it's due to the fact that Switzerland is one of the expensive countries in the world. And if you're an average salary man from another country, then wasting money is not an option. Anyway, the main reason why we were there was to visit the border between three countries, France, Germany and Switzerland. We actually expected that the place will be crowded but to our surprise, nobody was there. Getting there is quite tricky and to the point of being sketchy, probably that's why. item.title: Granville, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Granville is a coastal town in the region of Normandy, northwestern France. We went there for the post-birthday weekend trip of Iris. We've also met up with friends and took a day trip to Les îles Chausey, a group of islands few hours by ferry from Granville. The city is small, so a day or two is enough to walk around, unless you want to stay for a little gambling in their casino. And for those who are into luxury items, you can visit Christian Dior's home. Although it was in the middle of a heatwave, don't get fooled by the sea. It was still cold AF. And since it is a coastal town, it is recommended to still bring a jacket because the wind could pick up anytime at night.  Also, and the most important thing, watch out for those nasty seagulls flying above you. item.title: Rome, Italy
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Go to Rome anytime but summer. We knew that there was a heatwave across Europe around that time but didn't realized it was that hot. We were able to visit Rome thanks Iris' voucher from her company. This was our first Italy trip together, my first time but her second time after she had a layover in Milan. You would expect to have goosebumps because of the history but it didn't happen because of the heatwave, obviously, but also of how dirty the city was. Piles of rotten garbage were everywhere. I'm pretty sure it was not like that everyday but that time was just exceptional. However, the main reason for my excitement of going to Rome was not the city itself, but what's in the city: Jollibee!!! As soon as we dropped off our things at the hotel, we headed directly to Jollibee. Over the next days, we also found some Filipino restaurants. Yes, no pasta and pizza. Shame, right? Well, we rather be shameless than having a toilet emergency in the middle of the street. :D We're both lactose intolerant. The heatwave was just the start of the things that went south on our trip. The worst is yet to come in the next few days. item.title: Vatican City
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: If you're a Roman Catholic devotee or an art connoisseur, the Vatican is definitely on your list. A city-state surrounded by Rome, Italy, is home to the Pope and a trove of iconic art and architecture. Every corner is literally both an art and history. St. Peter's Basilica is already worth the visit but the Sistine Chapel's ceiling and Raphael's rooms should not be missed. If you've been listening to your history teacher or just casually browsing the internet, I'm pretty sure you've heard of the Renaissance artists and this is the place. For years, I only saw them on TV back home halfway around the globe when the local TV station covers the election of the new Pope or during Christmas. And now, I'm standing in that same place. It felt surreal. However, the goosebumps went away and turned into a panic in a split second after we received a notification that our flight back the next day was canceled for no reason and all other flights were already booked. Our option was to stay for a few more days in Rome and miss work or go to another city and fly from there. Obviously, missing work was not a choice. Our trip to Rome was supposedly cheap because of the gift card Iris received from her company but due to the canceled flight, it quickly became the most expensive trip. :P [caption id="attachment_6013" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] I'm not sure but this is probably the dome of St Peter's Basilica[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6014" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Our tour guide trying to rotate this metal globe[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6015" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Laocoön[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6018" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Art like this is all over the museum. item.title: Turin, Italy
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: The last leg of our sudden road trip twist was Turin. It is the only Italian city closest to France that has an available flight going home and of course, the only option we had considering our budget limit. Since we're already here, why not check out the city? So we booked a train a day before our flight and spent a night in Turin. As it turned out, there is a Filipino restaurant in Turin which is for us, comforting even after all the fuckery that had happened. So we went straight ahead and enjoyed a home-cooked Filipino meal. The city is relatively small compared to Rome. We spent the next day walking around the city. We ended up finding a covered market and boy oh boy, it is indeed true to find a pot of gold at the end of a rainbow. Calamares, deep-fried sardines, and pasta with mussels for days! Anything food? Sign me up. Seafood? Even better! Late in the afternoon, we were already on our way to the airport because we don't want to miss our flight. We can't afford to stretch our already extended vacation. And of course, unsurprisingly, the flight was delayed for 2 hours. We arrived home late and très pauvres. item.title: Luxembourg, Luxembourg
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
Today, we're going to talk about our recent short trip to Luxembourg, a charming country located in the heart of Europe. We started our journey from Metz, France, which is just a short distance away from Luxembourg. We hopped on a train and arrived in Luxembourg City in no time. As soon as we got off the train, we realized that we had forgotten an important fact about Luxembourg's public transportation system: it's free! Yes, you read that right. Public transportation in Luxembourg is completely free, which was a pleasant surprise for us. However, we didn't know this at first and panicked when we couldn't find a ticket machine as the tram was arriving. We thought we might get into trouble for not having a ticket, but then a friendly local informed us of the free transportation policy. What a relief! As soon as we arrive in the city center, we headed to the Old Town, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. We wandered through the narrow streets and marveled at the stunning architecture of the buildings, many of which date back to the Middle Ages. We also visited the Grand Ducal Palace, which is the official residence of the Grand Duke of Luxembourg. Sadly, he wasn't home when we visited, so we couldn't invite ourselves in for tea. Before we headed back to Metz, we stayed at Place des Martyrs to kill the time while waiting for our train. And here comes the good news: nobody stole my phone, even though I accidentally left it on the bench. It just goes to show how safe and secure Luxembourg is as a travel destination. Overall, our short trip to Luxembourg was a wonderful experience. We enjoyed the beautiful sights, the friendly people, and the great food. And best of all, we didn't break the bank, thanks to the free public transportation. So if you're looking for a unique and affordable travel destination in Europe, be sure to put Luxembourg on your list. And remember, don't panic if you can't find a ticket machine – public transportation is free!

item.title: Lille, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
Lille is a charming French city located in the Hauts-de-France region, just a short distance away from the Belgian border. It is a city with a rich history and cultural heritage, and its charming cobblestone streets, stunning architecture, and delicious food make it a must-visit destination for travelers to France. If you're planning to visit Dunkirk or Ghent, Lille is an excellent base to explore the surrounding areas. With frequent train connections to both cities, you can easily make day trips from Lille and return to the city in the evening. However, Lille is more than just a stopover destination. The city has a lot to offer in terms of attractions and activities, and you'll be pleasantly surprised by what you find here. One of the top attractions in Lille is the Citadelle de Lille, a military fortress built in the 17th century. The citadel is now a public park and a popular spot for locals and tourists alike. You can take a leisurely stroll through the park, enjoy a picnic, or take a guided tour of the citadel to learn about its history and importance. If you're a fan of art, you won't want to miss the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille (Lille Museum of Fine Arts). This impressive museum houses a vast collection of art from the Middle Ages to the 20th century. You'll find works by renowned artists like Rubens, Van Dyck, and Monet, as well as lesser-known artists that are just as deserving of your attention. And, of course, no trip to Lille would be complete without indulging in some delicious French cuisine. The city is known for its waffles, and you'll find plenty of places to enjoy them in Lille. Whether you prefer your waffles with powdered sugar, Nutella, or fruit, you won't be disappointed. Overall, Lille is a charming city with plenty to offer visitors. Whether you're using it as a base for day trips or staying for a few days to explore the city itself, you'll find plenty to keep you entertained. From its stunning architecture to its delicious food, Lille is a city that's sure to leave a lasting impression on you.

item.title: Dunkirk, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
Nestled on the beautiful coast of northern France, Dunkirk holds a significant place in history. A short train ride from Lille takes us to this coastal gem, ready to explore its rich history and picturesque landscapes. As we arrive in Dunkirk, we are greeted by the gentle sea breeze and the expansive coastline stretching before us. The sandy beaches invite us to take a leisurely stroll along the shore and listening to the soothing sounds of the waves. The beachfront promenade offers stunning views of the North Sea, making it a perfect spot for a peaceful moment of reflection. One of the pleasant surprises in Dunkirk is its free transportation system within the city. Hop on the sleek and eco-friendly buses that effortlessly take you from one corner to another, allowing you to explore the city's different facets with ease. This thoughtful initiative makes it convenient for visitors to navigate Dunkirk and experience its diverse offerings. As we delve deeper into Dunkirk's history, we encounter an unexpected revelation. Contrary to my previous misconception, Dunkirk was not directly linked to the D-Day landings during World War II. Instead, it played a crucial role in the early years of the war when the Allies faced a challenging situation known as the Dunkirk evacuation. During World War II, Dunkirk witnessed the extraordinary evacuation of hundreds of thousands of British and Allied soldiers in 1940. With the German forces advancing, the Allies orchestrated a daring rescue mission to evacuate their troops from the beaches of Dunkirk. This monumental operation, code-named "Operation Dynamo," involved a vast array of vessels, from naval ships to civilian boats, heroically transporting the soldiers to safety. To better understand the significance of the Dunkirk evacuation, we visit the Dunkirk War Museum. The museum offers a comprehensive insight into the events of 1940 through its captivating exhibits, personal accounts, and artifacts. Walking through the recreated wartime scenarios, we gain a deeper appreciation for the bravery and resilience displayed during those challenging times. Our day trip to Dunkirk proves to be a fascinating journey filled with historical discoveries, breathtaking coastlines, and a newfound appreciation for the bravery shown during the Dunkirk evacuation. Dunkirk's blend of captivating history, natural beauty, and culinary delights makes it a destination worth exploring. As we bid farewell to this coastal town, we carry with us the stories of resilience and heroism that define Dunkirk's place in history.

item.title: Ghent, Belgium
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
Upon arrival in Ghent, we're greeted by the tantalizing aroma of chocolates (yeah, chatGPT exaggerates sometimes). The city is a paradise for chocolate lovers, with numerous artisanal chocolatiers offering mouthwatering treats. We are not really chocolate people but we gave in. We bought couple of chocolate bars, specially those lactose free ones. Ghent's beer scene is equally impressive, with cozy pubs (one of which is literally adjacent to a church, coincedence?) and beer houses inviting us to sample a wide variety of brews. Cheers to that! As we explore Ghent's picturesque streets, we notice something refreshing – despite the crowds, the city maintains a relaxed vibe. We wander past medieval architecture, charming canals, and bustling squares, enjoying the atmosphere without feeling overwhelmed. Ghent knows how to handle a crowd without losing its cool. Ghent embraces its quirky side, adding a playful touch to the cityscape. Quirky street art surprises us around every corner, from amusing statues to witty murals that bring smiles to our faces. Ghent's charm lies in its ability to blend eccentricity with a laid-back attitude, creating a unique and enjoyable experience. Our day trip to Ghent is a lighthearted journey, filled with chocolate indulgence, beer appreciation, and a relaxed ambiance. Ghent's ability to offer a perfect blend of culinary delights, quirkiness, and a laid-back atmosphere sets it apart. As we bid farewell to this vibrant city, we carry fond memories of a fun-filled day in Ghent, where chocolates, beers, and a relaxed vibe reign supreme.

item.title: Nantes, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
Nantes, a captivating city in western France, became the backdrop for an eventful weekend getaway. Despite the challenges posed by an ongoing train strike in France, we went on a memorable exploration of Nantes' old town and captivating attractions. Though the strike incurred additional costs, the experiences we encountered made it a worthwhile adventure. We embarked on a leisurely stroll through Nantes' charming old town, soaking in the atmosphere of its narrow streets and historic architecture. Amidst this picturesque setting, we visited Les Machines de l'île, a unique and imaginative world where mechanical creatures roam. The sight of the towering mechanical elephant and the intricate carousel left us in awe of the city's artistic spirit. Nantes also holds a significant historical legacy, as evidenced by the Memorial to the Abolition of Slavery. This poignant monument served as a powerful reminder of the city's role in the transatlantic slave trade. We paid our respects, reflecting on the past and appreciating the progress made towards equality and justice. The train strike in France did pose challenges, increasing our expenses. However, we embraced the circumstances and made the most of our time in Nantes. Our day concluded with a satisfying brunch at Melbourne Coffee, and we bid farewell to the city, heading back to Paris with fond memories in our hearts.

item.title: Barcelona, Spain
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded:
Barcelona, a city I had eagerly awaited visiting, exceeded my expectations in every way. From savoring Filipino cuisine to exploring famous landmarks and enjoying panoramic views, this Spanish destination captured my heart. Craving a taste of home, we savored familiar Filipino flavors in Barcelona. From classic adobo to sinigang and halo-halo, each bite brought a comforting reminder of our homeland amidst the adventure. Barcelona's coastal location provided an abundance of fresh seafood. We indulged in a seafood extravaganza, relishing succulent prawns, tender octopus, and flavorful fish dishes. We immersed ourselves in Barcelona's iconic tourist spots. Exploring the Gothic Quarter, we marveled at medieval architecture and charming plazas. Gaudí's masterpieces, including Casa Batlló and Sagrada Família, left us in awe. We ascended to Tibidabo, Barcelona's highest point, for breathtaking panoramic views. From the summit, we gazed upon the cityscape, coastline, and distant mountains. Tibidabo's historic amusement park added an extra touch of magic to the experience. Barcelona fulfilled my long-held desire to explore its wonders. Filipino flavors offered a taste of home, while the city's seafood delights tantalized our palates. Immersing ourselves in famous landmarks and capturing panoramic views from Tibidabo created memories to last a lifetime. Barcelona truly exceeded expectations, leaving an indelible mark on our hearts.

Santa Maria de Montserrat Abbey, nestled amidst the stunning Montserrat mountain range just a short distance from Barcelona, beckons travelers seeking a unique and awe-inspiring experience. Embarking on a day trip from Barcelona, we ventured to Santa Maria de Montserrat Abbey, a spiritual and cultural gem. The abbey's location amidst the rugged and picturesque Montserrat mountain range offered a serene and rejuvenating escape from the city's hustle and bustle. Overcoming my initial apprehension, I challenged myself to embrace the cable car and funicular rides that transported me to the abbey. As I ascended through the awe-inspiring mountain landscape, a sense of triumph and wonder enveloped me, making the journey itself a memorable part of the experience. Nestled within the abbey complex, we discovered a delightful buffet restaurant offering a delectable array of dishes. From traditional Catalan cuisine to international flavors, every bite was savored while enjoying the stunning panoramic views that stretched as far as the eye could see. It was a feast for the senses, where gastronomy and breathtaking scenery seamlessly merged. A visit to Santa Maria de Montserrat Abbey from Barcelona is a captivating day trip that combines spiritual exploration, breathtaking views, and culinary delights. Overcoming fears on the cable car and funicular ride, I reached the abbey and immersed myself in its tranquil ambiance and rich history. The dining experience with panoramic vistas added an extra layer of delight, making the journey to Santa Maria de Montserrat Abbey an unforgettable and cherished memory.

item.title: Troyes, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: An hour away by train east of Paris is a small town called Troyes. We didn't have any idea about it until our friend Hannah brought it up and invited us for a weekend trip. An hour later, we arrived at the train station without any expectations. Having visited multiple European cities and small towns, I guess it's because of that, we are not totally overwhelmed by the medieval vibe of the town anymore. However, surprises are still there. Well, maybe if you don't set any expectations, there will always be room for surprises. The medieval old town features narrow, cobbled streets lined with colorful, half-timbered houses, mostly dating from the 16th century. But what fascinates me was the calmness of this town. It has a relaxed and chill vibe. Or maybe it was just because it is a small town. Or I had a good meal? And good sleep? Or no life problems at that time. Aaaahhh shit... this blog just made a sharp turn into the abyss. :P Anyway, there's more to France than Paris. Troyes is one of them. item.title: Amsterdam, The Netherlands
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Amsterdam once again. The last time we were in the city was 5 years ago. The reason why we went the back to the city is different than before. I attended a two-day conference held in the city but we extended our stay for one more day to explore city. We haven't had the chance to do it from the first visit due to the rain. We didn't ride bikes nor took a boat tour. We had too much bike rides during our first visit. We did walk around the city center, visited the Heineken Experience, chilled at the canal bank and a quick visit to a coffee shop. But we mostly spent our extra day at the Straat museum: an installation of arts by street and graffiti artists. If you are into graphic arts, you should definitely pay a visit at the museum. That was pretty much it! :D And man, this city is expensive. From our hotel to restaurants. Unlike in France, there is no une carafe d'eau for free. You had to pay an extra bottle of water or bring your own water bottle and refill it at the water fountains found around the city. After Amsterdam, we were off for our vacation in Mallorca. item.title: Mallorca, Spain
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: When I was at a conference in Amsterdam, there was one German speaker who developed a system for an insurance company. He jokingly mentioned that they have a specific type of insurance called Mallorca coverage. Mallorca is part of Spain and the biggest of Balearic Islands located in the Mediterranean. Apparently, Germans love spending their vacations on this island. In fact, he didn't lie. After we settled in our hotel, it was very evident that Mallorca is indeed one of the top destinations for Germans. Most of the shops have signage in German. German football teams all wearing their jerseys singing out loud in every bars. If you're a German, you would definitely feel as if you didn't leave Germany. However, we went there for two reasons: sea and seafood. The sea was okay. We are from the Philippines, so you know what I mean. ;) But that paella at Calixto's was something. I should have ordered the meat paella because munching at those crab shells was not fun. However, the taste was absolutely chef's kiss on Calixto's forehead. It was really that good! Damn! On top of that, you will receive the warmth and enthusiasm of Calixto with his broken English. Well, we didn't actually knew his name but we just assume that he is the owner of the restaurant. I love that guy. Aside from eating, we went to different places on the island. From Palma, we visited Soller and took an old train to Port de Soller. We also moved to the other side of the island and rented a scooter to drive around Alcudia and Polenca. It was my first time driving in another country. I was nervous but I had fun. One thing that's extremely commendable in the island's old towns was the cleanliness and coziness of it, specially Alcudia and Polenca. Overall, it was a pleasant experience. Nice places, good food and a much needed sea therapy. However, it was also the time where I unlocked my fear of flights. Small turbulence shoots up my anxiety. o.O [caption id="attachment_6250" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] In front of Catedral de Palma de Mallorca[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6251" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Random instagrammable alley in Palma[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6252" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Ajuntament de Palma (Hôtel de ville)[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6256" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Ensaïmada de Mallorca[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6253" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Boutiques in Palma[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6254" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Orange garden in front of Calixto's restaurant[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6258" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] The best paella I've tasted[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6260" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Sant Jaume d'Alcúdia[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6259" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Roman theatre (Teatre romà de Pol·lèntia)[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6249" align="aligncenter" width="1200"] Train going down to Port de Soller[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6257" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Town of Soller[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6248" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Port de Soller[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6262" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Another cozy old town in Polenca[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6263" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Outside Església Santa Maria de Pollença[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6264" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Cala Carbó[/caption]

item.title: Rouen, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Located northwest of Paris, Rouen is a port city of the river Seine. The city has Gothic churches such as Saint-Maclou and Saint-Ouen, and a cobblestoned pedestrian center with medieval half-timbered houses. But probably, the city is mostly visited for its Cathédrale Notre-Dame, much-painted by Impressionist Claude Monet and the Le Gros-Horloge, a 14th-century astronomical clock set on a Renaissance arch with detailed carvings. This is just another one of those weekend trips we had, thanks to the well connected railway networks in France, city like this is just few hours from Paris. As usual, Iris did all the planning while I just tagged along. >.< The main reason why we stayed in Rouen was its accessibility to Étretat, a coastal town north of France. If you've seen the French series Lupin, you might be able to recognize it. But we'll talk more about it on another post. :P Anyway, Rouen is a small city and with limited time, we just wandered around taking pictures, getting lost a little bit on narrow streets, and comme d'habitude, looking for food. item.title: Étretat, France
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: When you talk about white cliffs facing the ocean, I can immediately think of places I've seen on the internet such as in the UK. But Iris knows more and she's been talking a couple of times about the one in Étretat. As I've mentioned from the previous post, you might be able to recognize it if you've seen the episode on Lupin. It's just a small town but surprisingly full of tourists. You are allowed to swim in the ocean (English Channel) at your own risk or climb up the cliffs and take pictures from above. There are signs warning tourists not to stay at the edge but of course, tourists (being tourists) mostly ignore these warnings. Having fear of heights helped us to stay on the safe side. :P We literally stayed there for just a couple of hours because, one, there's nothing else to do there and second, if we miss the bus going back to Rouen, we have to stay one night in town to wait for the next bus the next day. It's best advised to rent a car so that you'll manage your own time. Overall, it was a nice short experience. And as mentioned many times before, I am a sea person and if you talk to me and "accidentally" mention the word sea? Stop talking. On y va ! item.title: Valleta, Malta
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Malta, an archipelago in the central Mediterranean between Sicily and the North African coast. In only three hour direct flight from Paris, one could be in a completely different scene: sun and sea. We love the sun and specially the sea but the main reason we visit the country was BTS. Yes, that K-pop group BTS. Iris is a big fan and this trip was inspired by one of the BTS' series shot in Malta. So there we went. We planned to visit few cities in the country and our first stop was Valleta, the country's capital. Of course we did what BTS did (some of it), strolling around the city and even eating at a restaurant called Cockney's where the owner pinned a picture of him and Jin on the wall. :P During our stay at Valleta, it was also around that time where they celebrate Notte Bianca, an annual celebration of arts and culture in Malta. There were parties in every corner, concerts and shows which we took part of for a couple of hours. Food was also another highlight of this trip. I'm a sucker for seafood and I was n the right place. We were eating fish and squid all the time. And surprisingly, we found a Filipino restaurant in one of their food halls. Of course we couldn't let it pass specially that sweet halo-halo. This is just our first city and we got more places to explore on this archipelago. item.title: Mdina, Malta
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Mdina is a fortified city in the northern part of Malta. It is also known as the Old City, which served as the country's capital until the medieval period. The city is still confined within its walls, with its few hundred inhabitants, including the cute cat that serves as a lookout at the gate. The walled city is small enough to walk around in just a few hours, including random stops to take pictures. However, you are not constrained to staying only within the walled city because Rabat, the town on the other side of the walls, also has a lot to discover. The island is rich in Roman history, and just a few blocks away from the Mdina gate, you'll find Domvs Romana, an open-air remains of a 1st-century BCE Roman house and a museum showcasing mosaics from the site. There is also St. Paul’s Catacombs, an ancient Roman underground cemetery complex. Both of which we visited. We spent the whole day in the city, with a huge part of it allotted to finding the bus station going back to Valletta. item.title: Blue Grotto, Malta
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Blue Grotto is another tourist destination in Malta. It is a complex of sea caves along the Southeastern part of the country. And again, I had no idea of its existence because it was Iris who did the planning, as always. 😎 I did know the country though. Memorizing country's capital was kind of my lunch in high school. 😏 The main attaction in Blue Grotto is a boat tour inside the caves but what I was really after is cliff jumping. I'm not good at it but I like doing it. And if you've been following my previous posts (most likely not), I've mentioned cliff jumping a couple of times before. Anyway, I did it on one of the not so high cliffs. The sea was a refreshing sight except for the giant jellyfishes everywhere. Although they are pretty safe to be in contact with but still, it's a little bit uncomfortable. 😬 After having too much food and a few hours of swimming, we went back to Valleta as early as possible. Missing the bus on the way back is not an option because the bus schedule is not as frequent as compared to other cities. If you happen to visit the place one day and want to spend more time in town, it is recommended to rent a car or a motorcycle. item.title: Gozo, Malta
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: On our last few days in Malta, we moved to the northern part of the island and stayed in a hotel to at least pamper ourselves before we go back to hustling again. Here, we were just less than an hour's ferry ride to Gozo island, the second biggest island in Malta. We spent a whole day exploring Gozo, half of it was on a hop-off/hop-on bus because of the intense summer heat. We wanted to rent a motorcycle but unfortunately they ran out of motorcycles for rent on that day. The remaining days were calm and spent mostly on enjoying the sea and a game of tag between us and a group of jellyfish, sometimes. It was a nice summer break, especially for someone who loves the sea. Relaxing. Good food. Nice weather. I would definitely go back there if there's a chance. But most probably, we'll prioritize visiting other places we haven't been to yet. I'm looking at you Portugal. *winks* [caption id="attachment_6371" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Solar panels on the roofs viewed from Rotunda St. John Baptist Church[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6372" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Uphill street in Victoria[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6373" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Touristing in Victoria[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6374" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Cathedral of the Assumption[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6375" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Ferry from Gozo to mainland Malta[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6376" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Comino Island[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6377" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Contemplating at the Coral Lagoon.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6378" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] It-Torri l-Abjad[/caption] [caption id="attachment_6379" align="aligncenter" width="1024"] Chilling at the shore keeping myself away from the jellyfish[/caption]

item.title: Singapore
item.dc:creator: jb.cagumbay@gmail.com
item.content:encoded: Singapore has long been on my list of countries to visit. Last year, I had the chance to go there with one thing on my mind: food. Everyone I know who has been to Singapore told me that the hawkers are a must-visit, and they didn’t disappoint. The hype met my expectations to the point where I brought jars of kaya back to France. Iris has a work colleague from Singapore who recently visited France, and yep, we asked for kaya. 😉 Another thing that lived up to the expectation was the humidity and heat. I told myself that I was prepared for it, but damn, it was humid AF. I was sweating as soon as we got out of the hotel. The only upside was that, unlike in the Philippines, there’s no smoke pollution from the cars. We stayed a couple of days in Singapore and met up with friends, Kristy and EJ. We did the regular tourist destinations. I even received a little surprise cake from the restaurant where we had dinner at the top of the Marina Bay Sands, which was nice. Before we left for Brisbane, we met up with Iris’ cousin to have dinner at Satay by the Bay before settling at the Gardens by the Bay to wait for the light show. After it, we had to call it a night to get some rest before our early morning flight to Brisbane.
